data.title: Calif. Governor Newsom prefers Warner Bros/Paramount settlement 'if it's a good deal'
data.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would like to see a settlement of the state attorneys general's lawsuit to block Paramount Skydance's (PSKY) $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) "if it's a good deal."

“That has to be worked through, and that’s a process that’s unfolding,” Newsom said Friday at a press conference in San Francisco, according to a Bloomberg account  of the event. “I’m concerned about the state, our reputation.”

Newsom's comments come after a WSJ report that Newsom was concerned about the state's suit to block the deal. Newsom is concerned that if the combination is blocked, it could have negative implications for employment in the state.  Newsom's office is encouraging Bonta's office to find a settlement outside of court. Newsom doesn't have any role in the litigation and doesn't have authority over the state AG's actions.

Earlier this month, Paramount (PSKY) CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the movie studio out of California if he couldn't reach a settlement with California's AG. Paramount (PSKY) would move the studio to Tennessee, Texas, Georgia, or another identified state if he can't reach a deal with California AG Rob Bonta by Oct. 1, according to a Puck News report. 

Newsom said at the press conference on Friday that he didn't think Paramount wanted to leave California, though he added that he was taking the possibility seriously.

“I hope that doesn’t happen, and I’m of the belief that they don’t want to see that happen,” Newsom said. “I’m talking about the future of the industry. I’m talking about Hollywood.”

On Wednesday, Cinemark  (CNK) became the latest movie theater chain to back the merger of Paramount (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), joining Regal Cinemas and AMC Theaters (AMC) in support of the deal.

Shares of Warner Bros. rose 1.1% on Friday, while Paramount edged higher by 0.7%.

data.title: FDA publishes new list of nicotine pouches authorized for sale in the U.S.
data.description:
On Friday, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration published a current list of the nicotine pouch products that are authorized to be sold in the U.S. While these pouches can be sold legally in the U.S., the agency does not consider them “safe” nor FDA-approved.

The pouches that have been approved for sale include on! nicotine pouches (2 mg, 6 mg PLUS) manufactured by Helix Innovations, a subsidiary of Altria (MO), and ZYN pouches (3 mg, 6 mg, 9 mg, and 11 mg ULTA) made by Swedish Match USA, a unit of Philip Morris International (PM).

This list includes 11 new nicotine pouches authorized for sale through the FDA’s premarket tobacco product application ((PMTA)) pathway. These 11 pouches are made by Swedish Match and sold under the ZYN ULTRA brand name.

The new list brings the total number of nicotine pouches authorized for sale to 43.

The FDA’s evaluation found that the new products, including the 11 mg product authorized today, contain lower levels of the most harmful and potentially harmful constituents when compared to other oral and smokeless tobacco products, many of which were too low to be quantified in the new products. 

Additionally, the review showed that the new products may deliver sufficient nicotine to reduce cravings and withdrawal systems “to a degree that can support behavioral change.”

Shares of Philip Morris International (PM) and Altria (MO) closed lower on Friday, ending the week down 1.1% and up fractionally, respectively.

data.title: S&P 500 drops 1.43% for week as Tech, Industrials lead sector losses
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages closed firmly higher on Friday, with Treasury yields largely steady and Bitcoin (BTC-USD)experiencing sharp intraday swings.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.9%, the S&P 500 (SP500) rose 0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.4%. 

However, the S&P 500 slipped 1.43% for the week.

Despite the weekly downturn, Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman maintained his bullish stance, saying, “Oil prices and rates rising at the same time are a double whammy for markets, but I don't believe that these are permanent fixtures. I remain bullish on the market despite this drop through the end of the year. This week's price drop largely came without a change in earnings, meaning that the market re-rated lower. In other words, it got cheaper, not worse.”

From a sector-level perspective, three S&P sectors ended the week in positive territory, while eight sectors finished in the red.

Health Care (XLV) and Energy (XLE) were the strongest-performing sectors this week, with gains of 4.40% and 2.89%, respectively.

Bowman saw a rotation into healthcare, energy, and materials as a cry from investors for defensiveness (which makes sense when you see tech and industrials as losers this week).

He also highlighted that healthcare was one of the worst performers this year before this past month, so there may be some mean reversion happening there; no doubt this may also be an idiosyncratic bump from the Moderna/Merck news about recent cancer vaccine success. As for energy, he would expect to see strength so long as the U.S.-Iran war keeps oil prices elevated, so no surprise there that it keeps chugging at a time like this.

Conversely, Technology (XLK) and Utilities (XLU) posted the weakest weekly performances, with losses of 3.47% and 3.43%, respectively.

“The duration trade hit equities hard as tech, industrials, and utilities sold off. With the recent news of Treasury buybacks at the long end and rates in flux, I can see how these sectors caught the ask this week. This also reads as broadly risk-off, but I'm writing that off for this week because of how other assets like Bitcoin have been behaving. Risk still seems very much on, but it took a breather this week in equities,” Bowman concluded.

data.title: Lake Ridge Bancorp Inc. GAAP EPS of $4.36

data.title: Wall Street ended higher as gold and Bitcoin rallied
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages closed firmly in the green on Friday, as Treasury yields held mostly steady and Bitcoin (BTC-USD) saw sharp swings. 

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) added +0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) closed +0.4%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, seven of the 11 S&P segments concluded in the green and were led by materials, while utilities suffered the most.

Treasury yields advanced. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.23%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was higher by 2 basis points to 4.73%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) ticked up 2 basis points to 5.27%. 

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) observed sharp swings Friday as the cryptocurrency extends a volatile rebound from below $64K earlier this week.

“Bitcoin and Ether has taken many by surprise; the short-squeeze dynamic in Bitcoin has been remarkable.  We believe there is plenty more upside in these categories yet,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

“After three weeks of strong performance, the S&P 500 is finally succumbing to the usual August volatility that we tend to see this time of year, driven by rising bond yields and confusion about the Treasury's bond purchase program. Bond yields are on the rise, and don't seem to be responding to the Treasury's purchases, largely because the bond market is massive and is pricing in a stronger economy and higher inflation,” Paul Stanley of Arca stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Robinhood Markets (HOOD) climbed higher by +13.7%, while shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) fell -5.4%.

data.title: OpenAI cuts API, credit pricing of GPT-5.6 Sol
data.description:
• OpenAI (OPENAI) said on Friday that it has cut pricing for its Application Programming Interface and credit of its latest frontier model, GPT-5.6 Sol, by 20% for the next three months.
  • The ChatGPT maker made the announcement on its X account.
  • GPT-5.6 Sol was released in limited preview in late June before rolling out on a broader basis last month.

data.title: Eaton initiated Outperform at Baird as 'just getting started' capturing AI demand
data.description:
Eaton (ETN) up 1.4% in Friday's trading as Baird initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and $500 price target, saying the power management company is "just getting started capturing AI demand," as cloud still represents most data center sales currently, but orders were 50% AI in 2025.

Baird analyst Luke Junk said Eaton (ETN) is well-equipped for the upcoming transition to800VDC, recent M&A has created a broad AI infrastructure platform, and the point of maximum operating pain amid once-in-a-generation capacity expansion has passed.

Eaton (ETN) is now on the downslope of a once-in-a-generation expansion across 24 ElectricalAmericas sites, with Q1-Q2 marking the largest production ramp in management's model and 18 sites now online, and the added capacity helped unlock exceptional ~220% Electrical Americas data center order growth, while 2026 also marks peak M&A digestion, supported by new and dedicated global data center leadership, the analyst wrote.

Rising aircraft production is a down payment on future aftermarket business, where higher content on key platforms, anticipated 25% revenue passenger-mile growth through 2030, and strong one-in-two commercial air penetration overall support durable growth in revenue and margin, while the aerospace business adds a growing $1B market opportunity, Junk said.

data.title: Tesla leads China’s record vehicle recall over door safety
data.description:
China has begun its largest vehicle recall, with Tesla (TSLA) and 10 other manufacturers addressing safety concerns involving emergency access to vehicle doors.

The campaign covers almost 4.3 million vehicles, highlighting the growing regulatory focus on electronic systems as automakers race to add new technology to cars. Tesla (TSLA) accounts for the biggest portion, with about 2.98 million Model 3, Model Y, Model S, and Model X vehicles affected.

The recall centers on the possibility that occupants or rescuers may struggle to find or use mechanical door releases after a serious crash, particularly if a vehicle’s electrical system stops working. Tesla (TSLA) plans to add identification labels and distribute a software update that can lower the windows following a collision.

Other affected manufacturers include Xiaomi (XIACF), Leapmotor (ZJLMF), Xpeng (XPEV), and Geely (GELYF). Xiaomi (XIACF) will cover about 390,000 vehicles, while Leapmotor (ZJLMF) and Xpeng (XPEV) are recalling roughly 371,000 and 264,000.

The measures come as Chinese authorities increase safety oversight of the world’s biggest auto market. Beijing has also announced plans to prohibit concealed door handles from 2027, a feature increasingly common in electric vehicles.

Most of the fixes will be carried out remotely, limiting the need for owners to visit service centers and reducing the expense associated with traditional recalls.

data.title: Alibaba-backed robot company seeks $3B value in new funding - Bloomberg
data.description:
Chinese robotics startup Dexmal is looking for a valuation of around 20 billion yen ($3B) in an ongoing funding round.

The talks are continuing and come after a previous round that included Chinese AI lab Z.AI Co., also known as Zhipu,  according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited an interview with  Dexmal founder Tang Wenbin at the World Robot Conference in Beijing. The fundraising follows rounds led by Alibaba (BABA) and NIO Capital late last year.

Chinese top humanoid robot maker Unitree surged more than fivefold in its stock market debut in Shanghai on Wednesday. Unitree—known for its robots that perform dance routines, martial arts, and backflips—raised about $900M in its IPO.

Unitree is backed by Chinese tech giants including Tencent (TCEHY) and Alibaba (BABA) as well as state-owned enterprises. Its U.S. competitors include Tesla (TSLA)  and Hyundai (HJMLF)-owned Boston Dynamics.
